mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen monotonically each of the last four weeks (-51.4 to -48.3), and this momentum reflects an ongoing unwinding of suppressed retail demand that will continue to push RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks absent any new shock.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved every week from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the mean over the last 28 days despite the four-week monotonic uptrend observed in this snapshot.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp week-on-week jump in PARKS mobility (-30.1 to -18.9, +11.2 points) signals households re-engaging in outdoor leisure activity; this outdoor-activity spillover typically extends into nearby retail and recreation visits within two weeks, lifting RETAIL_REC.

evidence_refs: fact:PARKS jumped from -30.1 to -18.9 between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise within two weeks following a PARKS jump exceeding 10 points, or declines despite the trigger condition being met.

mechanism_narrative: Joint improvement in TRANSIT (-49.6 to -45.6) alongside stable WORKPLACES (around -46.7) indicates that non-commute transit usage (shopping, errands, leisure trips) is driving the transit recovery rather than commuting; this combination predicts continued RETAIL_REC growth over four weeks because transit gains are not being absorbed by workplace travel.

failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth stalls or reverses even though TRANSIT continues improving while WORKPLACES remains flat, indicating the transit gains are not retail-linked.

mechanism_narrative: The steady decline in RESIDENTIAL (13.0 to 11.1) combined with improving RETAIL_REC and GROCERY_PHARM indicates an active policy-driven reopening phase (reduced stay-at-home restrictions in Lombardy's regional tier system); under this regime, continued relaxation should keep pushing RETAIL_REC upward over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 13.0 to 11.1 over four weeks while RETAIL_REC and GROCERY_PHARM both improved
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next four weeks even as RESIDENTIAL continues to decline, implying the reopening-regime linkage does not hold.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-May seasonal warming in Lombardy increases outdoor and retail foot traffic independent of policy changes, as reflected by the concurrent rise in PARKS and RETAIL_REC; this seasonal effect should persist and continue lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:both PARKS and RETAIL_REC show upward movement in the most recent week of this mid-May snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC and PARKS decouple, with RETAIL_REC falling over the next four weeks despite continued seasonal warming assumed from the May date.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has steadily improved each week (-22.4 to -18.6) and, as a less-restricted essential activity, acts as a short-horizon leading indicator of broader consumer willingness to leave home for non-essential retail within one week.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved each of the last four weeks from -22.4 to -18.6
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week immediately following continued GROCERY_PHARM improvement, breaking the presumed leading-indicator relationship.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has been essentially flat for four weeks (-46.7, -46.7, -46.1, -46.7), suggesting persistent remote-work policy or capacity restrictions on offices; if this stagnation continues or deepens, it signals an underlying restriction regime that will cap retail recovery by limiting weekday foot traffic near office districts within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES changes by less than 1 point week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES stayed within a 1-point band across all four observed weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to rise over the next two weeks despite WORKPLACES remaining flat, indicating office-based foot traffic is not a binding constraint.

mechanism_narrative: The joint pattern of rising TRANSIT (-49.6 to -45.6) and falling RESIDENTIAL (13.0 to 11.1) indicates a broad normalization of out-of-home mobility across multiple trip purposes; when both signals move together in this direction, it compounds into stronger retail recovery over four weeks than either series alone would predict.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose 4 points while RESIDENTIAL fell nearly 2 points over the same four-week window
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth over the next four weeks is no stronger than would be predicted from TRANSIT or RESIDENTIAL alone, or RETAIL_REC declines despite both series moving in the mobility-normalizing direction.
